name: NILM seq2seq: worst-device episode F1 on UK-DALE house_1
objectiveLabel: Target: every device F1 > 0.7 (episode-level, frozen 6 s protocol)

description:
Baseline v1: multi-house pretrained multi-output dilated CNN (house_2+house_5 sources, 80/20 train/val, 40k train + 8k val windows, window 128, stride 32, batch 512, 5 epochs, LR 1e-3, masked MSE + weighted BCE with per-device pos_weight kettle 34.1 / microwave 50.0 / fridge 1.3 / washing_machine 50.0 / dishwasher 1.0).

Eval: house_1 post-split 30d slice, frozen episode protocol (thr half_p50, >=2-sample episodes, tau 12e6 us, dwell_band (1/3, 3.0)).

Per-device (n_gt / n_pred / F1 / MAE_W / nMAE):
kettle 299 / 0 / 0.000 / 14.6 / 0.0425
microwave 262 / 0 / 0.000 / 7.3 / 0.0214
fridge 28034 / 0 / 0.000 / 40.0 / 0.1166
washing_machine 2966 / 0 / 0.000 / 27.9 / 0.0813
dishwasher 1353 / 0 / 0.000 / 17.0 / 0.0495
pooled F1 0.000; coverage pred=0.000 vs true=0.258.

Diagnosis: training collapsed in epoch 0 - train_mse 2724.57 -> 1.13 flat, val_mse_scaled frozen at 0.05416 across all 5 epochs, BCE noisy (389->110->64->48->85). Model outputs all-zeros (coverage_pred_share=0). Also: RuntimeWarning invalid value in divide at model.py:163 predict overlap-mean (cnt=0 windows -> NaN) - robustness bug to fix.

Next: stabilize training (grad clip, LR 3e-4, more epochs) before i2 calibration fine-tune.
title: EXP-01: multi-house pretrain baseline collapses to zero
summary: All 5 devices n_pred=0; training collapsed in epoch 0 (train_mse 2724.6->1.13, val_mse frozen 0.05416). Baseline min_device_f1=0.

asi.hypothesis: i1: multi-house pretraining (house_2+house_5) transfers zero-shot to house_1 eval under the frozen episode protocol.
asi.rollback_reason: n/a - baseline run, kept to anchor the segment.
asi.next_action_hint: Training-stability fix before i2: gradient clipping, LR 3e-4, 15+ epochs; fix NaN divide at model.py:163 (cnt=0 windows). Then calibration fine-tune (K=5 sessions).

description:
i1b training-stability iteration on top of baseline 54cf23b. Changes applied to model.py (exact recipe for re-application):
1. INPUT_SCALE=1000.0: mains watts divided by 1000 both in build_pool training inputs and in predict() input pad (descale unchanged: core*max_w - core is in normalized device units).
2. Power head clamp min=0.0, max=1.5 (target range).
3. Grad clip: torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(net.parameters(), 1.0) after backward.
4. LR 1e-3 -> 3e-4, EPOCHS 5 -> 12 (batch 512 unchanged).
5. NaN fix in predict overlap-mean: safe = np.where(cnt>0, acc/np.maximum(cnt,1), 0.0).
6. Added train-end diagnostics print (power head + on-head activity on 2048 val windows).

Result: training no longer collapses. Epoch trace: train_mse 0.13-0.26, bce 9.5->7.95 declining, val_mse_scaled 0.0039-0.0105 (10x below the v1 frozen 0.05416). Diagnostics: power head mean=0.124 max=1.31, on-head mean=0.32 max=1.0.

Per-device (n_gt / n_pred / match / P / R / F1 / MAE_W / nMAE):
kettle 299 / 30 / 12 / 0.400 / 0.040 / 0.073 / 15.6 / 0.0454
microwave 262 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.000 / 7.4 / 0.0215
fridge 28034 / 2 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.000 / 40.0 / 0.1166
washing_machine 2966 / 1 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.000 / 27.9 / 0.0814
dishwasher 1353 / 1851 / 10 / 0.005 / 0.007 / 0.006 / 27.0 / 0.0788
pooled F1 0.001; coverage pred=0.106 vs true=0.258. mean_mae_w 23.57 (vs 21.36 baseline - slightly worse), worst 40.0 (fridge, unchanged).

Diagnosis: heads are imbalanced across devices - dishwasher hyperactive (1851 preds vs 1353 gt, P=0.005), fridge channel effectively dead (MAE 40.0 = predicting ~0 despite 26% positive rate and pos_weight 1.3). Points to source->target transfer mismatch in per-device output levels, which is exactly what i2 (calibration fine-tune on the K=5 ctx sessions) is designed to fix.

Discarded per loop contract: min_device_f1 0 -> 0 (tie, no primary improvement). The recipe above + this description fully specify re-application.
title: EXP-02: stability fixes revive training, min-device still 0
summary: Input kW scaling + grad clip + LR 3e-4 + 12 epochs: training healthy (val_mse 0.005 vs 0.054 frozen), kettle F1 0.073, dishwasher 0.006; fridge n_pred=2 keeps min_device_f1=0.

asi.hypothesis: Stability fixes (input /1000 kW scale, head clamp 1.5, grad clip 1.0, LR 3e-4, 12 epochs, NaN guard) revive training and lift episode F1 off zero for some devices.
asi.rollback_reason: min_device_f1 tie 0 -> 0; contract keeps only primary improvements. Re-apply recipe from description in the next iteration.
asi.next_action_hint: EXP-03 = re-apply the 6 stability changes + i2 calibration fine-tune (K=5 ctx sessions per device) to fix the dead-fridge / hyperactive-dishwasher transfer mismatch. Consider i13 threshold snapping on predict if fine-tune alone is insufficient.

description:
i2 calibration fine-tune on top of re-applied stability recipe (v3 model.py). Stability changes re-applied exactly as documented in run 2 (INPUT_SCALE=1000 input kW scaling in build_pool + predict, head clamp min=0/max=1.5, grad clip 1.0, LR 3e-4, EPOCHS 12, predict NaN guard cnt=0 -> 0).

i2 design: after pretraining, fine-tune the WHOLE net on the K=5 target-house calib sessions per device (25 windows total, each supervising only its own device channel; other channels masked). FT_LR=1e-4, FT_EPOCHS=40, batch 32. Calib data: house_1 PRE-SPLIT (no eval leakage - verified bench.py line 250 pre = load_house(TARGET_HOUSE, None, SPLIT_US)).

Calib window stats: kettle on-frac 0.16, microwave 0.09, fridge 0.76, washing_machine 0.72, dishwasher 0.84 (observed-frac 0.82-0.90).

Fine-tune trace: calib_loss 12.66 -> 1.60 over 40 epochs (memorized the 25 windows). RETENTION DAMAGE: pretrain-val MSE 0.00623 -> 0.07144 (11.5x worse). Calib-fit MSE 0.048.

Per-device (n_gt / n_pred / match / P / R / F1 / MAE_W / nMAE):
kettle 299 / 303 / 39 / 0.129 / 0.130 / 0.130 / 33.9 / 0.0988
microwave 262 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.000 / 7.3 / 0.0214
fridge 28034 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.000 / 40.0 / 0.1167
washing_machine 2966 / 849 / 128 / 0.151 / 0.043 / 0.067 / 43.3 / 0.1262
dishwasher 1353 / 2011 / 39 / 0.019 / 0.029 / 0.023 / 91.8 / 0.2677
pooled F1 0.011; coverage pred=0.448 vs true=0.258 (over-prediction). mean_mae_w 43.26 (worse than EXP-02 23.57), worst 91.8.

Findings: (1) Target-house adaptation lifts episode F1 for kettle (2x) and washing_machine (new) - the transfer-mismatch hypothesis is directionally right. (2) Weight-space fine-tuning on 25 windows overfits and wrecks overall calibration (MAE doubled, coverage over-predicts 0.448 vs 0.258). (3) Fridge (n_pred=0) and microwave (n_pred=0) stay dead through BOTH stability fixes and fine-tune - not purely a fine-tuning problem.

Discarded: min_device_f1 tie 0 -> 0. Next hypothesis: keep the stable pretrained net UNTOUCHED (no weight fine-tune) and calibrate the per-device OUTPUT SCALE from the calib sessions (least-squares watts scale on observed calib positions, clamped) - attacks the level mismatch without weight drift; plus diagnostics printing per-device predicted-watts p95 on ON positions vs the frozen threshold to measure how far dead heads are from firing.
title: EXP-03: i2 calib fine-tune helps some devices, overfits
summary: Fine-tune on 25 calib windows: kettle F1 0.073->0.130, wm 0->0.067, but pretrain-val MSE 0.006->0.071 (11x retention damage), MAE 23.6->43.3. Fridge+microwave still 0 -> min_device_f1=0.

asi.hypothesis: i2 weight fine-tune on K=5 calib sessions adapts per-device output levels to the target house and lifts episode F1.
asi.rollback_reason: min_device_f1 tie 0->0 AND fine-tune overfits (retention MSE 11x worse, MAE doubled) - weight-space adaptation on 25 windows is the wrong vehicle; output-space calibration is the fix direction.
asi.next_action_hint: EXP-04 = stability recipe (no weight fine-tune) + per-device output-scale calibration from calib (least-squares on observed positions, clamp [0.5, 4.0], applied in predict descale) + diagnostics: per-device pred p95 on ON positions vs frozen threshold. If fridge head has no signal at all, next target the fridge head directly (source-data audit / dedicated head loss).

description:
i9 output-scale calibration on top of the stability recipe (v4 model.py; no weight fine-tune). Stability changes identical to runs 2-3 (documented there). New: per-device least-squares watts scale from calib sessions r_d = sum(p*q)/sum(p*p) on observed positions, clamped [0.5, 4.0], applied in predict descale (core * max_w * r_d); plus calib diagnostics printing per-device predicted-watts p95 on ON positions vs frozen threshold.

NOTE: ft_pretrain_val_mse_pre/post are 0 here = NOT APPLICABLE (v4 dropped the whole-net fine-tune; those metrics belong to the v3 design). washing_machine_f1=0.0 is real (1 predicted episode, 0 matches).

Calib diagnostics (the key evidence):
kettle r=1.08 pred_p95_on=3206W true_p50_on=2331W thr=1173W (ALIVE, over-amplitude)
microwave r=1.00 pred_p95_on=0W true_p50_on=1588W thr=762W (DEAD)
fridge r=1.00 pred_p95_on=0W true_p50_on=90W thr=44W (DEAD)
washing_machine r=1.00 pred_p95_on=0W true_p50_on=1778W thr=90W (DEAD)
dishwasher r=1.00 pred_p95_on=2672W true_p50_on=122W thr=60W (ALIVE, fires everywhere)

Result: scales all ~1.0 - multiplicative calibration cannot revive a head that outputs exactly 0W. Per-device table ~= EXP-02: kettle 38 preds F1 0.077, fridge 2, washing_machine 1, microwave 0, dishwasher 1853 F1 0.006. min_device_f1=0, mean_device_f1=0.0167, mean_mae_w=23.60, coverage pred=0.108 vs true=0.258.

Root-cause analysis (from diagnostics + loss structure): (1) The MSE amplitude gradient scales with normalized ON amplitude - fridge ON target is 90/2048=0.044 (negligible gradient) vs kettle 2331/3996=0.58 (strong) -> amplitude-starved heads die. (2) The ON head IS alive (train-end diagnostics: sigmoid mean 0.32 max 1.0) but predict() DISCARDS it (p, _ = net(xb)) - detection is currently expected from the MSE power head alone, which is the wrong vehicle for rare/small devices. (3) Dishwasher fires on everything (P=0.005) - no OFF suppression mechanism in the watts path.

Discarded: min_device_f1 tie 0 -> 0. Next hypothesis (EXP-05): head-role separation - route detection through the ON head: train power head with MSE masked to device-ON positions only (amplitude where it matters; Adam handles the small fridge targets), keep class-balanced BCE for the ON head, predict watts = max_w * core_power * gate(sigmoid(on_logit) > per-device gate threshold calibrated on calib ON/OFF sigmoid quantiles). Diagnostics: per-device gate ON-p05 vs OFF-p95 separation on calib.
title: EXP-04: output-scale calib inert; dead heads measured at 0W
summary: Calib least-squares scales all ~1.0 (dead heads have no signal to scale). New diagnostics: microwave/fridge/washing_machine pred p95 ON = 0W vs true 1588/90/1778W. min_device_f1 still 0.

asi.hypothesis: Per-device least-squares output-scale calibration from calib sessions fixes the level mismatch without weight drift.
asi.rollback_reason: Scales all ~1.0 - dead heads (pred exactly 0W on calib ON positions) have no signal to rescale. Calibration fixes live-but-miscalibrated heads only. min_device_f1 tie 0->0.
asi.next_action_hint: EXP-05 head-role separation: MSE masked to ON positions (amplitude head), BCE ON head as detector, predict watts = max_w * core * hard gate on sigmoid(on_logit) with per-device gate threshold from calib ON/OFF sigmoid quantiles. If gate separation is poor for a device, next lever: robust per-device normalization (p95 instead of nanmax) to un-starve small-amplitude gradients.
